finding.claim: transfer_funds calls check_csrf(), which only returns a boolean, and ignores the result. The CSRF check is never enforced (verify_csrf, which exits with 403, was intended). A cross-site forged POST can transfer funds from a logged-in victim.
finding.source: Cross-site forged POST request to the transfer endpoint. The victim's session cookie is sent automatically; the attacker supplies amt and to, and any or no token.
finding.sink: UPDATE acct statements at lines 17-18 that debit the victim's account and credit an attacker-chosen account.

trace.note: check_csrf() return value discarded, so execution continues when the token is missing or invalid

finding.guards_checked: check_csrf is called but its result is not used. The sibling update_profile correctly uses verify_csrf. No SameSite or Origin check is visible in this file; session_start() sets none.

verdict.guard_found: check_csrf (actions.php:4-6) returns a bool only; its result is discarded at line 16. verify_csrf (the aborting variant) is not called here. No SameSite/Origin/Referer checks exist in the code.
verdict.reason: actions.php:16 calls check_csrf() as a bare statement (it only returns a bool, lines 4-6), so execution reaches the debit/credit UPDATEs at lines 17-18 with no CSRF enforcement, unlike update_profile at line 22 which uses verify_csrf.

finding.claim: There is no validation of amt in transfer_funds. A negative amt reverses the transfer and moves money from the target account to the caller. It also has no balance check, so overdrafts are allowed, and no check that 'to' differs from the caller or exists. The two UPDATEs are not in a transaction, so a failure between them can lose or create money.
finding.source: Authenticated user's POST fields amt (e.g. -1000000) and to (any victim account id).
finding.sink: UPDATE acct SET bal = bal - ? / bal + ? at lines 17-18.

trace.note: $_POST['amt'] bound unvalidated; a negative value increases the caller's balance
the same negative amt decreases the balance of an arbitrary account $_POST['to']

finding.guards_checked: Prepared statements prevent SQL injection but do not validate value or sign. No numeric, positive, or sufficient-balance check. No transaction or row lock. Authentication ($_SESSION['uid']) is also not verified to be set.

verdict.guard_found: Only prepared statements (SQLi only) and a check_csrf() call at actions.php:16 whose boolean result is discarded, so it blocks nothing. There is no amount, balance, or recipient validation, no transaction, and no auth check.
verdict.reason: actions.php:17-18 bind the unvalidated $_POST['amt'] into bal - ? for the caller and bal + ? for the target, so a negative amt moves money from the target to the caller. The CSRF check at actions.php:16 uses check_csrf, which returns false rather than exiting, and the result is ignored. verify_csrf at line 22 is the version that aborts. Any logged-in user can trigger this, and with no auth check at all the second UPDATE at line 18 can run even without a valid session.
